title: Chapter 2 Revision — Motion Verbs
description: Mixed revision quiz covering chodzić/iść/pójść, jeździć/jechać/pojechać, running, flying, and motion verbs in context.

questions.prompt: Codziennie ___ do pracy pieszo. (Every day I walk to work on foot.) [habit, foot]
questions.explanation: Daily habit on foot → 'chodzę' (chodzić, multidirectional). 'Idę' = I'm going right now. 'Pójdę' = I will go once. 'Codziennie' = signal of habit → use multidirectional verb.

questions.prompt: Przepraszam, gdzie ___ teraz? (Excuse me, where are you going right now?) [ongoing foot motion]
questions.explanation: 'Idziesz' = you are going right now (iść, unidirectional, present). 'Chodzisz?' = Do you usually go? (habit). 'Pójdziesz?' = Will you go? (future, single event).

questions.prompt: Wczoraj ___ do Gdańska samochodem. (Yesterday I drove to Gdańsk.) [single past vehicle trip]
questions.explanation: 'Pojechałem' = I drove (perfective, single completed trip). 'Jechałem' = was driving (ongoing, background). 'Jeździłem' = I used to go / habitually drove. 'Wczoraj' + single trip = perfective.

questions.prompt: Uważaj! ___ samochodem przy czerwonym świetle! (Watch out! He's driving through the red light!) [right now, vehicle]
questions.explanation: 'Jedzie' = he is driving (right now, jechać, unidirectional, 3rd sg). 'Jeździ' = he drives habitually. 'Pojechał' = he drove/went (completed). The warning is about right-now dangerous action = unidirectional.

questions.prompt: Uwaga! ___ na autobus, który za chwilę odjedzie! (I'm running for the bus that's leaving in a moment!)
questions.explanation: 'Biegnę!' = I'm running right now (biec, unidirectional, urgent present action). 'Biegam' = I run habitually. 'Pobiegłem' = I ran (past perfective). Urgent present situation = unidirectional.

questions.prompt: Często ___ do Londynu służbowo. (She often flies to London for business.)
questions.explanation: 'Lata' = she flies habitually (latać, multidirectional, 3rd sg). 'Leci' = she is flying right now. 'Poleciała' = she flew (once, past perf). 'Często' = signal of habit → multidirectional.

questions.prompt: W narracji: 'Jan ___ do parku, a potem przez godzinę ___ alejkami.' [ran to / ran around]
questions.explanation: Narrative: 'Pobiegł do parku' (perf — arrived at the park) then 'biegał alejkami' (imperf multidirectional — ran around the paths). Classic perfective arrival → imperfective activity pattern.

questions.prompt: 'Jechałam autostradą, kiedy...' — what type of verb is 'jechałam'?
questions.explanation: 'Jechałam' = imperfective past of jechać (unidirectional — ongoing vehicle motion, one direction). It functions as background for a kiedy + perfective event. 'I was driving when...' = imperfective background.

'Wsiadać/wsiąść do + gen' = to get on/in (a vehicle). 'Wsiadłam do autobusu' = I got on the bus. Contrast: 'Wysiadać/wysiąść z + gen' = to get off/out. Polish uses do (in) for getting in, z (from) for getting out.

questions.prompt: Jutro ___ do lekarza — mam wizytę o jedenastej. (Tomorrow I'll go to the doctor — I have an appointment at eleven.)
questions.explanation: 'Pójdę' = I will go (perfective, single future event). One specific appointment → perfective. 'Idę' = I'm going right now. 'Chodzę do lekarza' = I go to the doctor regularly (habit). 'Jutro' + one event = perfective.
'Po drodze' = on the way (fixed phrase). 'Kupię mleko po drodze' = I'll buy milk on the way. Very common: 'Czy możesz wziąć po drodze...?' = Can you pick up [something] on the way?

questions.prompt: What does the prefix 'przy-' add to a motion verb (przyjść, przyjechać)?
questions.explanation: 'Przy-' = arrival / coming toward the speaker or destination. 'Przyjść' = to come (on foot), 'przyjechać' = to arrive (by vehicle). Contrast: 'od-' = going away, 'prze-' = passing through, 'wy-' = going out.
